newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower Thursday, pressured by continued declines in pork values and an increase in hog movement, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for slaughter hogs delivered to Iowa and southern Minnesota plants were seen ranging from $48.00 to $49.00 and Illinois top prices at the plant could span $47.00 to $47.50, dealers and packer buyers in those areas said.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range $48.00 to $48.50, sources there said.

The interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog run Tuesday was 106,000 head, compared with the 105,000 estimate, USDA said. Wednesday's estimate was 110,000 head, compared with 111,000 a week ago and 108,000 a year ago, USDA said.
The brisk hog marketings were expected to keep pressure on pork prices, which have been falling amid sluggish demand, dealers said.
Fresh pork loins at midday were quoted with a weak undertone, hams were steady to mostly $2.00 per cwt lower, pork bellies were steady and lean trimmings were steady to $1.00 lower, USDA said.
A total of 34 loads of pork cuts and 20 loads of trimmed and processed pork were reported sold, USDA said.
